blog_summary: The blog post discusses DeepCS, a code search engine that uses deep learning to bridge the semantic gap between natural language queries and source code snippets. Unlike traditional tools like Lucene or CodeHow, DeepCS employs the CODEnn (Code-Description Embedding Neural Network) model to learn a joint embedding space where code snippets and their corresponding natural language descriptions are mapped to similar points. This allows the system to understand the semantic meaning of both queries and code, enabling more accurate searches. The author highlights DeepCS's ability to handle complex queries, such as finding where events are queued on a thread, and its superior performance over existing tools. The paper also details the architecture of CODEnn, which includes separate embedding networks for code (using RNNs and MLPs) and descriptions (using RNNs), and a similarity module based on cosine distance. Evaluation on a large corpus of Java methods and Stack Overflow queries demonstrates DeepCS's effectiveness, though it occasionally ranks partially relevant results higher due to its reliance on semantic vectors alone.
paper_abstract: 1 To implement a program functionality, developers can reuse previously written code snippets by searching through a large-scale codebase. Over the years, many code search tools have been proposed to help developers. The existing approaches often treat source code as textual documents and utilize information retrieval models to retrieve relevant code snippets that match a given query. These approaches mainly rely on the textual similarity between source code and natural language query. They lack a deep understanding of the semantics of queries and source code. In this paper, we propose a novel deep neural network named CODEnn (Code-Description Embedding Neural Network). Instead of matching text similarity, CODEnn jointly embeds code snippets and natural language descriptions into a high-dimensional vector space, in such a way that code snippet and its corresponding description have similar vectors. Using the unified vector representation, code snippets related to a natural language query can be retrieved according to their vectors. Semantically related words can also be recognized and irrelevant/noisy keywords in queries can be handled. As a proof-of-concept application, we implement a code search tool named DeepCS using the proposed CODEnn model. We empirically evaluate DeepCS on a large scale codebase collected from GitHub. The experimental results show that our approach can effectively retrieve relevant code snippets and outperforms previous techniques. Code search is a very common activity in software development practices [57, 68]. To implement a certain functionality, for example, to parse XML files, developers usually search and reuse previously written code by performing free-text queries over a large-scale codebase.
